text: Every video must have a proper thumbnail/cover, and its text must hedge exactly like the narration (same qualifiers, no stronger claim than the voiceover makes).
evidence: black-october: Owner: 'Every video needs a proper thumbnail... The cover must hedge exactly like the narration.' | retired: the cover is made by frameflow.cover, whose prompt already requires the narration's hedges

text: Keep a single ending beat after the payoff (one closing question or one practical takeaway, not both stacked) and a short tail (about 10 s or less); fold any extra stat into the scene before. Never write a follow call to action: the pipeline's end card adds it.
evidence: black-october: Owner: 'an outro call to action (follow)'. Review: three endings run back to back in the 18s tail after the payoff.; again in black-october; again in 2026-10-25-black-october (Talha's feedback)

text: Never leave a frame near-empty while the narrator is speaking: every key phrase (stat, rating, quote intro) needs its visual on screen from the first frame and held until the line ends. Check keyframes at each narration cue for blank pages.
evidence: black-october: Scene 5 at 29s faint kicker only during 'rated nine point', Scene 8 blank page at 43s during 'Chainguard's CEO says', cake missing before Scene 6, and Scene 10 sky text appearing early over the wrong line.; again in black-october; again in 2026-10-25-microsoft-develops-ai-tool-that-can; again in 2026-10-25-black-october (Talha's feedback)

text: When revising a script, keep the first draft's voice, jokes and rhythm; fix only what the notes name. In a blind test the owner preferred the first draft over the final revised one.
evidence: black-october: blind A/B on 2026-10-25, Talha chose script-v1 over script (final).

text: Make the script flow for a first-time viewer: every part should lead into the next, and when the story moves on, the viewer should know what is being answered now and why. Use whatever fits the moment (a spoken question, a 'but' or 'so', a callback, a quick bridge) and vary it; never just jump to an answer the viewer wasn't set up for.
evidence: black-october: Owner: some questions are asked aloud ('The cause?') while others appear only as an on-screen heading and the narrator jumps into the answer. It should be consistent so the audience can follow.; again in 2026-10-25-black-october (Talha's feedback)

text: Time each reveal visual to its narration cue and in the storyboard order. Show the big number, the object or the quote card on the cue word, hold it until the line ends, and don't show later text early.
evidence: black-october: 'RATED 9.2' caption didn't render at 'rated nine point'. The 14-candle cake never showed. The sky said 'NOT EVEN YOU' from 57s, before 'Not you'.; again in 2026-10-25-microsoft-develops-ai-tool-that-can; again in 2026-10-25-black-october (Talha's feedback)

text: After the payoff, run one ending beat only. Fold any extra stat into the preceding action scene rather than adding another closing scene, and keep the tail after the payoff short (about 10s or less).
evidence: black-october: Pacing: three endings ran back to back (Censys stat, to-do note, finders-or-fixers question) in an 18s tail after the payoff. | merged into L2

text: Keep the picture in step with the voice: headings, labels and on-screen questions should match what is being said at that moment and help the viewer follow where the story is going, not introduce a question or point the narration never makes.
evidence: black-october (Talha's feedback): 'HOW COMMON IS PHP?' and 'HOW BAD? HOW OLD?' were shown as headings while the narrator jumped straight to the answers; other questions were asked aloud. Pairs with L5.; again in 2026-10-25-microsoft-develops-ai-tool-that-can

text: Give the headline stat its own dominant visual: show the big number large on screen on the cue word and keep both compared numbers visible together until the line ends, with props that make the setting readable (e.g. two labelled desks with score sheets). Never leave the key number tiny or absent.
evidence: 2026-10-25-microsoft-develops-ai-tool-that-can: Scene 8: no 83.2% on screen while the voice says 'eighty-three point two'; only a tiny 36.1% shown at 53 s.; again in 2026-10-25-black-october (Talha's feedback)

text: Change the on-screen note or visual on every clause of the narration, and don't let one scene's overlay fall back to a single note. Check that no stretch over 2.5 s repeats the same frame, especially the opening seconds, and that no blank frame sits before the end card.
evidence: 2026-10-25-microsoft-develops-ai-tool-that-can: Hook frames at 1–7 s were the same street; scene 14 notes never appeared; blank frame at 91 s; failed events check with 3.1 s gap and rehook 10.6 s.

text: Put sound accents on the biggest moments: every riser must resolve into an impact on the key number or reveal, and thin out whooshes/pops in busy scenes (no more than about one SFX per 2 s) so the peak stands out.
evidence: 2026-10-25-microsoft-develops-ai-tool-that-can: Riser at 46.8 s had no hit and 83.2% at ~49.5 s got no accent, while scenes 3–5 fired SFX every ~2 s.; again in 2026-10-25-black-october (Talha's feedback)

text: Give each scene only one new fact, and when the video runs longer, add a bridge line that links the previous fact to the next instead of adding another fact.
evidence: 2026-10-25-black-october (Talha's feedback): Owner said the script feels like it jumps between sentences and information is delivered too fast, and that the video length limit can be raised if the pacing stays calm.

text: Leave about 0.5 s of clean silence directly before any twist or big reveal impact, with no whoosh, tick or other effect in that gap, so the peak lands on air.
evidence: black-october review: Review sound_plan: the 62.8 s scratch was to be followed by about 0.5 s of clean silence before the 64.2 s impact-big so the twist lands on air, not on a run of effects.
